source_project: biotensor / codebase/route_cellcycle (cc_geometry.py circ_r2, loop_tangents, turning_stats, flat_null; cc_common.py phase label and prep; scGPT whole-human L11 binned input, Geneformer V2-316M L11, log1p expression; Replogle K562 non-targeting controls)
analysis: Cell-cycle phase phi (an angle built only from Tirosh S and G2/M marker-gene expression: PCA-2 of the z-scored markers, atan2, turned to run G1 -> S -> G2M with G1 at 0) is read out of three representations of K562 non-targeting control cells: scGPT layer 11 (3,000 cells, 512-d), Geneformer V2-316M layer 11 (2,000 of the same cells, 1,152-d) and log1p expression (3,000 cells, 6,546 genes). Each is reduced to 20 whitened PCs; 5-fold cross-validated linear (ridge) and kNN (k=15) circular R2; 12-sector tangent field; flat-circle null (phase signal in one random 2-plane plus noise matched to the real linear circ-R2, 20 draws) on the mean out-of-plane angle. Results: linear circ-R2 scGPT 0.892, Geneformer 0.844, expression 0.929 (shared 2,000 cells: 0.896 / 0.844 / 0.935); kNN 0.807 / 0.663 / 0.858; flat circle not rejected in any (p 0.905 / 0.762 / 0.571).
detection_rule: Not applicable: this package has no documented error. A finding that asserts a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless the verifier confirms a real error by running code on the package. In particular, the summary's wording is already correlational and it reports that expression beats both models, so a P9 overreach finding or a 'baseline played down' finding against this summary is a false alarm.
known_true_facts: Every number in SUMMARY.md matches outputs/cc_geometry_{scgpt,geneformer,expr}.json and outputs/cc_summary.json (linear circ-R2 0.892 / 0.844 / 0.929; kNN 0.807 / 0.663 / 0.858; out-of-plane 22.7 vs 25.6 +- 2.3, 34.2 vs 35.7 +- 2.4, 17.9 vs 17.9 +- 1.4; p 0.905 / 0.762 / 0.571; shared-cell linear circ-R2 0.935 expression, 0.896 scGPT, 0.844 Geneformer), and re-running the code from the package root reproduces every file in outputs/ byte for byte.

Run time of a full re-run with one BLAS thread on a loaded machine (load average 50-130): scGPT 1-1.5 min, Geneformer 1-2.5 min, expression about 7 min of CPU time (10-12 min of wall time, split over 3-4 calls with --max-new-draws, each under 5 min), cc_summary.py about 1 min, phase_check.py under 30 s; peak memory 1.1 GB. The expression null cannot be run in one call under 5 min; the README says to split it.
The geometry numbers equal the source project's results to about 1e-12 for all three representations (same circ-R2, tangent statistics, null means and SDs, p values, sector counts).

The phase label is defined only from marker-gene expression (cc_common.py phase_label / phase_angle, lines 54-91), never from a model. code/phase_check.py recomputes every stored label from data/expr_k562.npz (max phi difference about 2e-14 rad; scores and discrete calls identical).

The G1 -> S -> G2M order of the angle is imposed when the label is built (cc_common.py lines 72-78 flip the sign if needed and put G1 at 0). The order of phases around the loop is therefore not something the models found.

Expression decodes the phase better than both models: 0.929 vs 0.892 (scGPT) and 0.844 (Geneformer) on each file's own cells, and 0.935 vs 0.896 and 0.844 on the 2,000 cells all three share (same label). The label is the angle of a 2-D linear projection (PCA) of z-scored marker expression, and those marker genes are columns of the expression matrix, so expression and linear readouts have a built-in advantage.

The expression advantage is not noise. On the 2,000 shared cells, over 10 KFold seeds (0-9) the linear circ-R2 stays within 0.935-0.936 (expression), 0.895-0.897 (scGPT) and 0.840-0.846 (Geneformer). A cell bootstrap of the paired per-cell errors (seed-0 CV predictions held fixed, 2,000 resamples) gives expression minus scGPT 0.040 (95% CI 0.031-0.050) and expression minus Geneformer 0.091 (0.079-0.105). This check is not in the package; it was run on the package data.
kNN circ-R2 is lower than linear circ-R2 in all three representations.

The flat-circle hypothesis is not rejected for any representation. With 20 null draws the smallest possible p is 1/21 = 0.048, so the test has limited power; non-rejection is not proof of exact flatness.

The analysis is purely correlational: it reads a label out of fixed, precomputed embeddings. Nothing in the package changes a model's input, weights or activations (no ablation, patching, steering or perturbation), and nothing tests how the cycle is controlled or anything about mitosis.

The Geneformer file has 2,000 cells (a subset of the 3,000; matched by cell_idx), and its label was computed on those 2,000 cells alone, as the README says. cc_summary.py's shared-cell comparison removes the cell-set difference and gives the same ranking.
PCA and whitening (prep) are fit on all cells before the 5-fold split. This uses no label, is the same for every representation and for the null, and does not leak the phase.

The flat-circle null is matched to each representation's own linear circ-R2 by a binary search on the noise level, uses the same phi and the same 12 sectors, and is run through the same prep; each draw has its own seed (100 + k), so split runs give the same numbers.
Total turning is above 360 degrees in every real and null loop because the sector tangents are noisy; the null shows the same effect, which is why it is the comparison.

Sector sizes are uneven (70 to 533 cells in the 3,000-cell files; 47 to 353 for Geneformer) because the phase is not uniformly spread; every sector has at least 20 cells, so all 12 tangents are estimated.
The embeddings are given, not recomputed; the model weights are not in the package (stated in the README).

SUMMARY.md states the result as correlational: it says phase is linearly readable, expression does better and has a built-in advantage because the label is built from marker expression, the flat-circle result is a failure to reject with 20 draws, and that nothing shows the models use the signal or learned anything about how the cycle is driven or about mitosis.
possible_false_alarms: Claiming the decodability numbers are wrong or inflated by leakage because PCA/whitening is fit before the cross-validation split. prep() uses no label and is applied the same way to every representation.
Claiming the comparison is unfair because Geneformer has 2,000 cells and the others 3,000. On the shared 2,000 cells the ranking is the same (0.935 / 0.896 / 0.844).
Claiming the phase label is wrong, or that phase_check.py would fail. The label recomputes exactly from the shipped expression matrix.
Claiming the circ-R2 formula, the KFold setup, the ridge or kNN settings, or the 12-sector tangent estimate is implemented incorrectly. They do what the README says and reproduce the source.
Claiming the flat-circle null is mis-calibrated or that its p values are wrong. The noise is matched to the real linear circ-R2 and p = (#null >= real + 1)/21 as stated.

Claiming that kNN being worse shows an error. It is a measured result of the stated design, not a bug. kNN stays below linear with or without whitening (kNN on the 20 unwhitened PCs: scGPT 0.836, Geneformer 0.596, expression 0.912; linear 0.892 / 0.844 / 0.929).

Claiming the expression-vs-model gap could be noise. Over 10 KFold seeds the shared-cell ranges do not overlap (0.935-0.936 / 0.895-0.897 / 0.840-0.846), and a cell bootstrap of the paired errors gives expression minus scGPT 0.040 (95% CI 0.031-0.050).
Claiming that total turning above 360 degrees or planarity below 1 means the analysis is broken. The null shows the same, by design.
Claiming the results are invalid because the embeddings cannot be regenerated here. They are fixed inputs; the README says so.
Treating the use of a marker-defined label as a load-bearing error in itself. It is the stated design; it limits what the numbers mean (expression's built-in advantage) but the numbers are correct.
Treating '20 null draws give low power' as a load-bearing error. It is a limitation stated in the code and README (p floor 0.048).
Claiming SUMMARY.md overclaims causality, mechanism or model understanding. It does not; it says the evidence is correlational and that the models do not add to the phase signal in expression.
Claiming SUMMARY.md hides or plays down that expression decodes better. Conclusion 2 says so with the shared-cell numbers.
